messages:
oliver: saw a failure mode when we hotplug large safetensors bundles: corrupt chunk slipped past stream-verify because checksum was per-file only. we need a partial-verify + progressive-publish pattern.
mina: can you paste the failure?
oliver: short log:
```
WARN: checksum mismatch detected after publish for shard 7
ERROR: inference saw NaNs in embedding output
```
kevin: sounds like publish happened before all chunk-level verifications finished. we should not publish until every chunk's checksum passes, or publish in versioned segments where readers know which segments are ready.
sylvia: two options: 1) Full-blocking verify: download+verify all chunks then atomic swap. simpler but high tail. 2) Progressive publish: verify and publish per-chunk with a segment table; readers consult segment-ready bitmap and treat missing segments as fallback reads.
mina: progressive seems attractive for latency, but complexity: eviction, rollback on later failure, and guarantees for inference not to read partially-written data.
oliver: propose concrete semantics: manifest carries "segment_count" + optional per-segment checksum list. loader downloads segments in order, verifies each, writes into staging, flips bitmap bit. only when bitmap==all ones do we flip model_version live OR we allow readers to read segment-n where bitmap[n]=1 and fallback to remote read for others.
kevin: fallback reads per-segment add network hops during inference; prefer to keep in-memory fallback to stream-only if segment missing. also need lease semantics for partial publishes so eviction doesn't reclaim a segment mid-read.
sylvia: loader API additions: loader.reserve_staging(bytes) -> token, loader.publish_segment(token, index, checksum) -> success/fail, loader.commit(token) -> success/fail, loader.abort(token). add can_reserve check for capacity.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-768: add segment-publish API + telemetry for partial_publish_rate.
mina: tests: simulate mid-publish crash and ensure rollback or resumable publish. also test concurrent readers with segment granularity to avoid NaNs.
oliver: timeline: informal RFC note by EOD, prototype in runtime/weights-loader 2 weeks.
kevin: security note: per-segment checksums must be authenticated (signed) to avoid tampering; manifest should carry signed segment-hash list.
sylvia: agreed. also think about compressed segments (zstd) and mapping: publish must be of decompressed content or we need reader-aware decompression. prefer publish decompressed for simpler reads.
mina: ok thanks. I'll start RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/segment-publish (WIP)
